synopsis: Risk tone is soft but not panicked this morning: US and European equity futures drift lower (S&P -0.2%, Euro Stoxx -0.3%) as Europe's political and fiscal woes dominate — Spain's premier called a snap election after failed housing votes, France's finances remain under scrutiny, and the euro has slumped to a 17-month low at 1.1245.
commentary:
Risk tone is soft but not panicked this morning: US and European equity futures drift lower (S&P -0.2%, Euro Stoxx -0.3%) as Europe's political and fiscal woes dominate — Spain's premier called a snap election after failed housing votes, France's finances remain under scrutiny, and the euro has slumped to a 17-month low at 1.1245. OAT and Gilt futures are underperforming Bunds, confirming the fiscal-premium story is in the periphery of the curve, not the front end. The other big overnight print is Brazil, where Flávio Bolsonaro's surprise first-round lead over Lula sent the real surging 4.6% as markets price a right-ward, market-friendly shift ahead of the runoff.

Fed pricing is steady with traders leaning toward a pause after the soft jobs report, even as Treasury's Bessent walks back comments after long-end yields kept rising; Takaichi's "rest assured" message on Japanese issuance hasn't stopped JGB long yields hitting fresh highs — the global long end remains the pressure point. In commodities, energy is the talking point: Brent holds above $102 after Aramco's chief warned global oil stockpiles are "scarily thin" and could take two years to rebuild, with Yemen fighting intensifying — though Saudi price cuts to Asia capped crude, leaving WTI softer while distillates ripped (gasoil +2.9%, heating oil +1.5%) on tight product supply.

Precious metals keep grinding higher — gold at $4,189, silver +2.5%, platinum +2.7% — the classic hedge against fiscal stress and a debased-currency narrative even with the dollar firm.
